note: NFU1 defects disrupt lipoic acid cofactor synthesis for the glycine cleavage system, causing hyperglycinemia in affected spastic paraplegia patients, unlike classical HSPs.

evidence.text: A patient with NFU1 mutation presenting with slowly progressive spastic paraparesis and leukoencephalopathy exhibited high glycine concentrations, highlighting hyperglycinemia as a key diagnostic clue.

evidence.text: A patient with homozygous NFU1 mutation presenting with spastic paraparesis had hyperglycinemia, reinforcing that elevated glycine is characteristic of NFU1-associated phenotypes.

source.title: A genetic mimic of cerebral palsy: Homozygous NFU1 mutation with marked intrafamilial phenotypic variation
source.quote: Hyperglycinemia and cavitating leukodystrophy are suggestive of an NFU1 mutation diagnosis.
